headline: Katahdin Parking and Camping Reservations
reservation: Baxter State Park requires specific Day Use Parking Reservations (DUPR) for popular trailheads like Roaring Brook. Camping must be booked well in advance through the park's own reservation system; check the official site as rules for Maine residents and non-residents differ.

days.title: The Ponds of the North Woods

stops.name: Sandy Stream Pond
stops.detail: Visit this iconic pond for a chance to see moose against the backdrop of the Katahdin massif.

stops.name: Daicey Pond
stops.detail: Explore the Nature Trail and view the historic library at one of the park's most scenic campsites.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours; the Park Tote Road is unpaved and limited to low speeds.
days.note: Moose sightings are frequent but never guaranteed; maintain a safe distance at all times.

days.title: Waterfalls and Forested Paths

stops.name: Big Niagara Falls
stops.detail: Take a moderate walk through the woods to reach these powerful falls on Nesowadnehunk Stream.

stops.name: Little Niagara Falls
stops.detail: A short distance from its larger neighbor, offering a different perspective of the rushing mountain water.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; road conditions vary with recent weather and maintenance.
days.note: Rocks near the falls are slippery; stay on designated paths for viewing.

days.title: The Great North Peak

stops.name: Baxter Peak
stops.detail: The northern terminus of the Appalachian Trail, reached via strenuous and technical hiking routes.

stops.name: South Turner Mountain
stops.detail: A shorter but steep alternative providing one of the best views of Katahdin's Great Basin.

days.driving: Minimal if parked at the trailhead; allow 10-12 hours for a full Katahdin hike.
days.note: A summit attempt is a major undertaking; check weather and turn back if conditions deteriorate.

days.title: North Park Wilderness

stops.name: Trout Brook Farm
stops.detail: Explore the quieter northern end of the park, known for its rolling hills and remote feel.

stops.name: South Branch Pond
stops.detail: Enjoy the dramatic scenery where the mountains drop directly into the water.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours to traverse the length of the Park Tote Road; conditions vary.
days.note: The northern gates are far from Millinocket; ensure you have enough fuel for the return trip.

intel.title: Mandatory DUPR System
intel.text: Parking at Roaring Brook, Abol, and Katahdin Stream is managed by a reservation system. Without a pre-booked slot, you may be turned away at the gate during peak summer months.

intel.title: Total Wilderness Disconnect
intel.text: There is no cellular service or Wi-Fi within the park boundaries. Communications are limited to ranger stations for emergencies only; carry paper maps.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: No fuel, food, or supplies are sold inside Baxter State Park. You must fully stock up in Millinocket or Patten before passing through the entry gates.

intel.title: Strict Gate Hours
intel.text: The park gates open and close at specific times; arriving after hours may prevent access to your campsite. Check the official seasonal schedule before your travel day.

intel.title: Vehicle Size Restrictions
intel.text: Large RVs and trailers are restricted on the Park Tote Road due to narrow dimensions and sharp turns. Verify your vehicle's length and width against park regulations.

plan.arrival: Fly into PQI and allow at least 3.5 hours for the drive to the park's northern gate; buy all food and camping fuel in Patten or Millinocket.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with high clearance is recommended for the unpaved Park Tote Road, though not strictly required; check rental terms for gravel road use.
plan.goldenHour: Sandy Stream Pond offers a classic view of Katahdin's peaks, though evening shadows fall early in the deep basins.
